paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. The psalm says, "Those who trust in the LORD are like Mount Zion. It cannot be moved; it abides forever." (Psalm 125:1) Notice what makes the picture work. The mountain doesn't hold still because it's tough and works out. It holds still because of what it is. When your trust rests on the LORD, you're standing on something that doesn't wobble, even on the days YOU do.

Then the psalm says, "As the mountains surround Jerusalem, so the LORD surrounds His people, both now and forevermore." (Psalm 125:2) That's not a promise for the easy weeks only. It says "both now and forevermore," so the LORD around you is not a seasonal special. So when life feels like it's closing in on you, remember who is already on every side of you, baker.

The psalm also asks the LORD to "Do good… to those who are good, and to the upright in heart." (Psalm 125:4) And it warns that those who turn to crooked ways, the LORD will banish with the evildoers. (Psalm 125:5) So this song isn't just comfort. It's a call to keep walking straight, because the LORD who surrounds His people is the One worth following. And it ends the way I want you to leave my bakery: "Peace be upon Israel." (Psalm 125:5)
